cards.explanation: The answer is without words, by how their wives live. Peter says even husbands who refuse to believe the word "…will be won over without words by the behavior of their wives" (1 Peter 3:1). No speech needed, friends. Their lives do the talking, and I think that takes a lot of quiet strength.

The answer is the inner disposition of the heart. Peter says beauty comes "…from the inner disposition of your heart…" (1 Peter 3:4). He's pointing past braids, gold and fine clothes to the inside, friends. Nobody can wrap that up in a box, and nobody can polish it either.

The answer is True. Peter calls it "…the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit…" (1 Peter 3:4). Hair gets messy and clothes wear out. I know a thing or two about edges getting worn down, friends. This kind of beauty doesn't fade.

The answer is God. Peter says the holy women of the past "…put their hope in God…" (1 Peter 3:5). That's where their hope went, and it's the best place to park yours too, friends. Hope parked anywhere else gets towed.

The answer is give way to fear. Peter says they are Sarah's children "…if you do what is right and refuse to give way to fear." (1 Peter 3:6). Doing right and refusing fear go together in that line, friends. Fear can be loud, but it doesn't have to win.

The answer is fellow heirs of the gift of life. Peter says to honor wives "…as fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life…" (1 Peter 3:7). Fellow heirs means they share in it together, friends. Nobody is standing on a higher shelf in that kitchen.

The answer is False. Peter says husbands should treat their wives well "…so that your prayers will not be hindered." (1 Peter 3:7). So the way a husband treats his wife is connected to his prayers, friends. Home life and prayer life aren't in separate rooms.

The answer is False. Peter tells them all to "…be like-minded and sympathetic, love as brothers, be tenderhearted and humble." (1 Peter 3:8). Nothing about keeping it all inside, friends. Those are meant to be shown to each other.

The answer is blessing. Peter says not to repay evil with evil or insult with insult, "…but with blessing…" (1 Peter 3:9). Somebody throws a jab and you hand back a blessing, friends. Now THAT will surprise them.

The two answers are tongue and peace. The quote says whoever would love life "…must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech." (1 Peter 3:10). Words get a lot of attention in this passage, friends. A little muscle, a big deal. Then it says "he must seek peace and pursue it." (1 Peter 3:11). Seek it AND pursue it. Peter doesn't tell them to sit around waiting for peace to show up.

The answer is the righteous. The quote says "…the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer." (1 Peter 3:12). He sees them and He hears them, friends. That's a good thing to know.
